note: Track home-and-colour, step 4: La as the minor home on one major scale's notes: a line that rests on Do and one that rests on La, a line against a drone on La, then a backing track whose chords come home to Do and then to La. The staffs carry solfège labels, the key is moves (any key) with a {{?key}} line, and each section has a feel to reach.

exercise.title: La as home: the minor home
exercise.why: A minor key uses the notes of a major key and comes to rest on La instead of Do, so the same notes sound minor once La is home.

cells.heading: Rest on Do, rest on La

cells.text:
The staff below shows {{=key}} major with its solfège names, and the notes under the lowest Do as well. Tap {{3}}, {{2}} and {{1}}, and stop: the line rests on Do.
Now tap {{1}}, {{7}} and the ringed {{6}} downward from that Do, and stop: the line rests on La.
Practice until you hear which of the two stops sounds major and which sounds minor.

Tap from the low {{6}} up to {{3}} on the staff below, and come back down to {{6}}. Then press Play under the staff to start the drone on La, and tap the same line against it.
Practice until La sounds like the note the line has to end on.

Press Play under the staff below to start the backing track: four bars that come home to Do, then four that come home to La, round and round. Hum the home note of each half, then tap {{1}} or {{6}} on the staff to check.
Practice until you can say "Do" or "La" as each half begins.
{{?key}}In another key the notes have other names, and the same seven notes still sound major when they rest on Do and minor when they rest on La.
